tagline.text: Hot springs and a zipline at the foot of a volcano in inland Pangasinan

location.label: Location
location.text: Balungao, Pangasinan, at the foot of Mount Balungao (Napudot barangay road)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (per person per day, depending on activities)

children.text: Balungao Hot Springs is a hot and cold spring resort at the foot of Mount Balungao in southeastern Pangasinan. With hot spring pools, a zipline and a roughly 45-minute summit hike in one place, it makes an easy day trip from Manila or Clark.
Balungao is a small municipality at the southeastern edge of Pangasinan, bordering Nueva Ecija to the south. It lies about
178km
from Manila and about
71km

from the provincial capital, Lingayen, so it points in a different direction from the beach itineraries of the northern Luzon coast. That is exactly why it is quiet: few foreign tourists come, and the mood is that of local families on a weekend outing.
The centerpiece is Mount Balungao, about

high. It is an extinct volcano, and PHIVOLCS classifies it as inactive. Hot and cold water rise together at its foot, so locals have used the place as a hot spring for a long time, and the resort now operating as Balungao Hilltop Adventure channels that water into its pools. It was originally called the Mt. Balungao Hot and Cold Springs Resort, and is said to have opened as Hilltop Adventure on September 8, 2011.

The appeal is that there is plenty to do once you arrive. Hot and cold pools, a zipline over the pools, four-wheel ATVs, mountain bikes and a short guided summit hike are all within one compound. The climb to the top takes about
45 minutes
, and from the summit you can see the Pangasinan plain and the surrounding mountains.

Note that fees and facilities change often and official information is hard to find online. The prices here are approximate figures cross-checked from a 2014 flyer, a 2018 hiking blog and a 2022 article, so confirm by phone or on site before you go. Many visitors say the food options are poor, so bring a packed lunch and snacks.
The resort has five pools in all: three for children and two for adults. Two of them are filled with hot spring water and the rest with cold water. The adult pools are described as roughly
and
deep, so weak swimmers should stay in the shallower areas. Do not jump straight into the hot water; let your body adjust gradually.
There is a
zipline that runs above the pools and a longer
1.4km
line. The longer one is advertised as the longest zipline in northern Luzon (Region 1). The short line flying over the pools is great for photos; see the cost table below for prices.
This short route starts behind the resort and reaches the top in about
45 minutes
. The path is steep and rocky, with forest almost to the summit, and the upper section turns grassy and gentler. A guide is said to be required, so check the fee at the entrance.

blocks.title: Walk to the spring source along the creek

children.text: Instead of climbing, you can take a short walk along the creek at the foot of the mountain to where the hot spring water emerges. You may see candle wax along the way, apparently left by locals honoring the guardian spirit of the mountain, so it is polite not to touch it when taking photos.

blocks.title: ATV, mountain bikes and bungee trampoline

children.text: ATVs are rented in
15 minutes
blocks, and mountain biking and a bungee trampoline are also advertised. Some facilities may not operate at certain times, so ask on arrival whether they are available.

blocks.title: Day-trip distance from Manila and Clark

children.text: It is about
178km
from Manila along an expressway route, so if you leave at dawn you can arrive before lunch, spend the day and return. From Clark it is even closer.

This is not a place crowded with foreign visitors like Boracay or El Nido; local families are the main guests. The usual scene is people eating packed lunches in cottages or under umbrella shade and playing in the water.

blocks.title: Combine with Manleluag and the waterfalls

children.text: Manleluag Hot Spring (Mangatarem), Canding Falls and Timangguyob Falls are said to be nearby. If you can spend more than a day, they are worth adding to the plan.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: Hot springs, zipline and a short hike

children.text: Leave Manila or Clark. From Manila, allow roughly
3–4 hours
including the expressways, and check traffic conditions locally.
Arrive at the resort, pay the entrance fee and claim a cottage or umbrella shade. Unpack and decide where to keep your packed lunch first.
While the sun is still mild, try the
zipline or the ATV first. The morning is better because the lines are shorter.
Have lunch. Around the resort there are only small shops selling snacks (sari-sari stores) and simple eateries, so eating the food you brought is the least stressful option.
Do the summit hike. Allow about
45 minutes
up and a similar time down, and go with a guide. Early afternoon is the hottest part of the day, but starting at this time still beats the midday glare.
Cool off in the hot spring pools. Many visitors say the soak after the hike is the most satisfying part.
Leave before dark. The expressway toward Manila can back up on weekend evenings.
Official opening hours could not be confirmed. Late afternoon closing is typical, but ask for the closing time at the entrance.

items.title: Overnight plan
items.subtitle: Relax in a room and enjoy the hot springs

children.text: Arrive as in the day trip and enjoy the zipline and the pools.
Finish the summit hike and the hot springs.
Use a resort cabana (
12 hours
rate, sleeping about four) or stay in Balungao or Rosales town. It is wise to buy food in town in advance.
Visit Manleluag Hot Spring or a nearby waterfall before heading back. Road conditions to the falls can vary, so ask locally for directions.

items.title: From Manila by car or rental car

children.text: From Manila take NLEX to SCTEx (Subic–Clark–Tarlac Expressway), then continue onto TPLEx (Tarlac–Pangasinan–La Union Expressway).

Exit at the Carmen toll plaza on TPLEx. Turn right onto the Rosales–Balungao–Umingan Road, then turn right again into the Napudot barangay road, which leads to the resort. "Napudot" means "hot" in Ilocano.
In your navigation app enter "Balungao Hilltop Adventure" or "Mt. Balungao Hot and Cold Springs". It is about
180km
from Manila.
Road works and tolls change often. Check the latest TPLEx announcements before you leave.
Take a Pangasinan-bound bus toward Rosales or Carmen from a bus terminal in Manila. No confirmed source gives specific bus companies or schedules, so check at the terminal.
From Rosales or Balungao town, transfer to a tricycle or a jeepney to reach the resort, which is said to be about
3km
from the town center.
The nearest airport is Clark International Airport (CRK). A rental car or chartered vehicle using SCTEx and TPLEx is the easiest option.
Travelers leaving from Manila Ninoy Aquino Airport (MNL) use the same expressway route, so choose according to your itinerary.
From Balungao town to the resort, a tricycle is the most practical choice. Fares are negotiated, and no fixed fare was confirmed.
Since transport thins out in the evening, arrange a round-trip hire in advance to be safe.
Balungao is a nearly flat area at about
above sea level. Annual rainfall is about
and the average daily high is around
, so soaking in hot water is more pleasant in the relatively cooler dry season.

In the rainy season (roughly June to October), the summit trail can be slippery and the creek can rise, so follow your guide's judgment. On weekends, holidays and Holy Week, local families crowd in and cottages are hard to get; weekdays are much calmer.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The best time for the hot springs and the hike. Weekends are crowded.
Good for swimming, but avoid hiking around noon and climb early.
The creek and trails can be slippery, so check whether the zipline and the hike are available first.

items.label: Entrance (adult)
items.note: ₱50 in 2014 and 2018 sources; some recent listings give a higher amount that includes environmental and insurance fees

items.label: Entrance (child)
items.note: For children up to about 1.2 m tall; confirm locally

items.label: Cottage (kubo or umbrella)
items.note: Umbrella shade about ₱100, kubo about ₱200 (per 2014 flyer)

items.label: Zipline 600 m
items.note: The longer 1.4 km line is priced separately; confirm locally

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

The resort has cabanas (rooms), but they are few and are rented in 12-hour blocks. To stay overnight, it is more realistic to look for lodging in Balungao town or Rosales. Names and prices change over time, so check the latest ratings in a map app.

Food is the weakest part. A 2014 visit report said the restaurant was lacking and there was little more than snacks and drinks from sari-sari stores, while a 2018 hiking blog mentioned several simple eateries (turo-turo) near the entrance. That suggests it varies by year, so bring plenty of packed meals, water and snacks and treat anything bought on site as a bonus. Instant noodles and a thermos of hot water can be surprisingly handy for families.
Confirm the latest fees and closing time by phone before you go. Reviews list different numbers, so check the current number in a map app.
Do not jump into the hot spring; put your feet in first and let your body adjust. Children, older visitors and anyone with a weak heart should be especially careful.
Bring a towel, a change of clothes, sandals and sunscreen. Non-slip shoes are best for walking along the creek.
The summit hike is short but steep and rocky. Some people climb in sandals, but sneakers are safer.
Bring plenty of water and food and take your trash back with you. Cottages are often taken in order of arrival.
Keep valuables on you in a waterproof pouch, and avoid leaving belongings unattended in the cottages when you can.
Hike with a guide, and do not touch local spiritual offerings such as candle wax seen along the creek path.
Fee and facility information relies on older sources. Operations may be suspended or prices changed without notice, so always check before you leave.
Staying in hot water for long can make you dizzy. Step out and rest from time to time.
Use the zipline and ATV only after checking the safety gear and instructions, and do not ride if you feel unwell or have been drinking.
In the rainy season the trails and creek are slippery and can rise suddenly. Avoid hiking on rainy days.
There are few restaurants and shops nearby, so prepare food, water and cash in advance. Cards may not be accepted on site.
Mount Balungao is classified as inactive, but rockfall is possible on the climb, so follow your guide's instructions.

A hot spring inside a protected landscape in Malabobo, Mangatarem, regarded with Balungao as one of Pangasinan's two main hot springs. It can be combined in a regional itinerary; confirm the location locally.
A major pilgrimage site in inland Pangasinan. It can fit into an itinerary in the same direction as the hot springs, but check travel time locally.
A riverside resort area in Nueva Ecija to the south. Treat it as a reference for a combined route with other areas.
Waterfalls mentioned as nearby attractions in the resort's information. Trails and water levels vary by season, so confirm locally.
